issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares LaunchedDropdownTower with an attribute maxHeight:int (and thus its constructor must accept this attribute after the superclass attributes). The solution's LaunchedDropdownTower implementation has no maxHeight attribute and its public constructor only accepts (String name, char abbreviation). This contradicts the specification and will confuse students (and fail automated checks) that expect a constructor parameter and getter for maxHeight.
issues.suggested_fix: Update LaunchedDropdownTower to include the subclass attribute in the constructor signature: public LaunchedDropdownTower(String name, char abbreviation, int maxHeight). The constructor should first accept superclass attributes (name, abbreviation), call super(name, abbreviation), then assign this.maxHeight = maxHeight. Add a public getter for maxHeight.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies LaunchedDropdownTower has a private int maxHeight attribute. The solution implementation is missing this attribute entirely (no field and no corresponding getter). This is a structural mismatch that prevents students from matching the UML and from using/getting the maxHeight value as required.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a private int maxHeight field to LaunchedDropdownTower, initialize it in the constructor (see previous fix), and provide a public getter (e.g., public int getMaxHeight()). Ensure the field is included in the constructor parameter list after the superclass attributes, matching the UML and exercise requirements.
